newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mixed, nearbys slump.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mixed, nearbys slump.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended mixed in light dealings on Monday, with commission house selling pressuring the nearby contracts, traders said.
Traders said short-covering by speculators and locals buoyed helped lift the most-active September contract off its session low of 162.10 cents per lb -- its lowest level in three months.

September arabicas ended at 165.70 cents, down 2.65 cents a lb on the day and just short of the session high of 166.50 cents. Spot July ended down 2.25 cents, to 185.25 cents, while the outer months closed up 0.35 to 2.25 cents.

New York coffee prices fell from the outset, after losses overnight in the London robusta market. Traders said weather forecasts calling for continued mild weather in top-grower Brazil weighed on sentiment.

U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said in an update on Monday that the warm ridge of high pressure recently dominating Brazil's coffee belt is expected to remain in the region for the next seven days.
Temperature levels should stay near to above normal, with lows expected to continue to range in the 50's to low 60's F (low to middle teens C), WSC said.

Traders also said the potential for a build in exchange-certified inventories continued to hang over the market. Stocks rose by 1,926 60-kg bags as of July 4, to 52,476 bags, the CSCE said after the close of business on Monday. An additional 35,930 bags were pending exchange approval.

In other news, the latest export figures from the International Coffee Organization (ICO) showed producing members' exports reached 81.75 million 60-kg bags in the 12 months to May 1997, up sharply from 73.02 million in the same 1996 period.

While some traders said the nearly 9 million-bag increase in exports was bearish, reflecting a less dire stock situation than many market participants had feared, other traders said the rise in exports was constructive because it pointed to increased consumption.
"The exports were very high, but they are being absorbed," said one trader. "I think consumption is better than people anticipated, especially in producing countries."

Another trader said that increased exports, which are only particially reflected in the recent modest build in consuming countries stockpiles, could be held by roasters or may be in finished goods, both of which are not reflected in inventory data.
Technically, traders said September faced near-term chart support at 162.00 cents, followed by 158.00 and 155.00 cents. On the upside, resistance was seen toward the 170.00 level.

The CFTC is due to release its next Commitment of Traders data after today's close. But with total open interest holding fairly steady recently at above 20,000 lots, traders expected the figures to show little change.
Turnover was thin, at an estimated 4,799 lots.
